newsitem.title: USA: Man charged in Illinois courtroom bombing.
newsitem.headline: Man charged in Illinois courtroom bombing.

text.p: A man charged with throwing a firebomb at a judge in his courtroom on Tuesday had lost a case before the same judge two years ago, police said on Wednesday.
John Ewing, 37, who was arrested on Tuesday night, was charged with arson, possession of an incendiary device and possession of such a device while committing a felony.
Gary Turner, chief deputy at the Champaign County sheriff's office, said Circuit Judge George Miller dismissed a suit in 1995 that Ewing brought against a supermarket.
While Ewing did not confess to Tuesday's attack, Turner said, he made comments critical of the judicial system. Ewing, whose last known address was in Peoria, Ill., was arrested at a motel.

The 69-year-old judge, who was presiding over a civil trial when the Molotov cocktail was tossed at him, escaped serious injury by diving under his desk as the flaming bottle bounced off him. He gashed his forehead as he took cover and needed several stitches to close the wound.

The ensuing fire virtually destroyed the wood-panelled, carpeted courtroom, causing an estimated $100,000 damage. The fire took 20 minutes to extinguish but officials said the 96-year-old courthouse suffered no structural damage.
